strategy: Buys the 30 S&P 500 companies returning the most cash to shareholders through buybacks and dividends, measured against their market value, in equal weights and rebalanced monthly.

desk_notes.note: Tonight's book is 30 new names picked on shareholder yield: dividends plus buybacks. Most are large buyback programs at companies whose shares have fallen, like Gartner (down 48% over 12 months), Salesforce ($25B debt-funded accelerated buyback), Trade Desk (down 90% from its peak), Omnicom and PayPal. Financials are 23% of the book (SYF, ACGL, EG, MTB, AIG, TFC). Information Technology is 20% and is mostly software and data (IT, CRM, FICO, GDDY, WDAY, PTC). Advertising, cable and media together make up another 13% (CHTR, OMC, TTD, CMCSA). Charter is vetoed: its Cox merger closed 2026-08-20 and gave Cox Enterprises about 26% of the combined company. That dilution is not in the trailing yield, and Charter ranked first on that figure. Workday is in reported buyout talks with Silver Lake, with no signed deal. The Stripe/Advent bid for PayPal ended 2026-08-27. GoDaddy faces a securities class action.

desk_notes.note: The book holds 30 equal-weight S&P 500 names chosen for high shareholder yield: companies returning large amounts of cash through buybacks and dividends relative to their market value. Financials are the largest sector at 23%, then Information Technology and Consumer Discretionary at 17% each, and Communication Services at 13%. Three names enter: Charter, NRG Energy and Equifax. Charter is vetoed because it completed its $34.5 billion purchase of Cox on Aug. 20, 2026, so its trailing figures no longer describe the combined company. Its 35% yield is also an outlier. NRG adds a utility, and NRG and Equifax are both near 52-week lows. General Mills, Southwest Airlines and PTC leave the book. Since Sept. 11, the paper book has trailed its benchmark, $93,986 against $100,237. The membership snapshot is 92 days old.

verdicts.reason: Charter closed its $34.5B acquisition of Cox Communications around Aug. 20-21, 2026. Its trailing-12-month buybacks, dividends and share count come from before the deal and do not match the combined company. A 35.4% shareholder yield is implausible and fits that mismatch.
Q2 2026 EPS missed, Morgan Stanley cut its price target, and the stock hit a 52-week low. NRG reaffirmed its 2026 guidance. No acquisition of NRG, delisting or restatement was found.

The stock fell on FHFA pressure over credit-bureau fees and is down 34% this year. That is regulatory and price news, not a reason to veto. No acquisition of Equifax, delisting or restatement was found.
